subject: Tenancy options and SLO expectations — quick follow-up
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Booth <claire.booth@meditech.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@meditech.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Tenancy options and SLO expectations — quick follow-up

Hi Claire / Tom —

Thanks again for making time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the right path: 

- Primary constraint: you mentioned handling PHI and wanting strict isolation from other tenants.
- Expected steady-state ingest: ~120 requests/min during business hours, with bursts to ~500 req/min for scheduled nightly jobs.
- Latency target: p95 <= 150ms for single-turn generation on the 4k context model; availability target: 99.9% externally facing SLA.

Questions we need to confirm to recommend a deployment mode:
1) Data residency: Will any workloads be required to remain on-prem only, or is VPC (private cloud) acceptable?
2) Audit windows: how long must logs/traces be retained for compliance? (e.g., 90 / 365 days)
3) Burst tolerance: Are you willing to accept temporary fallbacks to a slightly smaller model during peak if we guarantee routing transparency?

Initial recommendation: Based on PHI + isolation ask, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools in your VPC or our private region) or Private (customer-managed VPC / on-prem) look most appropriate. Hosted API would need additional compensating controls (strong encryption, strict routing policies, dedicated tenancy add-on) to meet your isolation bar.

Proposed next steps:
- Claire: send back the security questionnaire from your IT team (you mentioned one) — that will let our security team validate any hosted exceptions.
- We can set a 45-min technical deep-dive (Rishi + infra) to map traffic profile to SKU sizing — are you available Fri 11 Sep, 10:00–10:45 PT?
- I'll attach an SLA/options matrix so you have an apples-to-apples view of tradeoffs (latency, cost, isolation).

Attached: SLA-options.xlsx (draft)

Thanks — happy to run the technical session and draft a mutual action plan.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Claire Booth <claire.booth@meditech.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:18:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenancy options and SLO expectations — quick follow-up

Thanks Jasmine — good recap. A few answers and clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency: For Phase 1, VPC deployment in our cloud account is acceptable (we use AWS us-west-2). On-prem only is not required now but we may consider it for future regulated workloads.
- Log retention: minimum 365 days for audit-related traces and token-level anonymized logs for 90 days.
- Burst tolerance: We prefer not to degrade model quality in production. If cost becomes a blocker we can discuss scheduled batch windows, but fallback to a smaller model must be accompanied by explicit runs to evaluate model-regression risk.

I've attached the Meditech security questionnaire (we use it to baseline vendors). You should find details on encryption expectations and SOC attestations there.

We like the idea of a Dedicated pool inside our VPC — isolation + predictable throughput sounds right. We're concerned about "noisy neighbor" effects from other tenants in multi-tenant hosts and want to understand guarantees around CPU/GPU allocation and noisy-eviction behaviors.

Availability: Fri 11 Sep at 10:00 PT works for the deep-dive. Looping in our infra contact Tom (cc'ed).

Attachment: MediTech_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf

—Claire
Claire Booth
Sr. IT Security Manager | MediTech Health
claire.booth@meditech.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Booth <claire.booth@meditech.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@meditech.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 11:02:10 +0000
Subject: Re: Tenancy options and SLO expectations — quick follow-up

Claire — thanks for the fast responses and for the questionnaire. I skimmed key sections and flagged a couple items for our security lead; we'll produce a formal response before the deep-dive.

High-level notes to address your noisy-neighbor / allocation questions before the call: 
- Dedicated pools: we can provision a dedicated GPU pool inside your AWS account (customer VPC) so compute never co-resides with third-party tenants. That covers the strongest isolation requirement.
- Isolation guarantees: Dedicated = dedicated host-level tenancy + exclusive GPU assignments per tenant. For Private on-prem, you control the entire infra. For Hosted with an isolation add-on, we offer tenancy slices with soft isolation and strong routing + KV caching separation but it doesn't give physical GPU exclusivity.
- Eviction & preemption: on shared hosts we use preemption thresholds and graceful KD/connection-draining; with Dedicated we avoid preemption entirely unless customers explicitly enable bursting.

Suggested technical deep-dive agenda (45 min):
1) Traffic profile + sample payloads (10 min)
2) Model selection -> latency estimates and perf curves (10 min)
3) Sizing & capacity (how many GPUs / reserved nodes) + cost estimation (15 min)
4) Security controls, audit logs & retention approach + next steps (10 min)

I've re-attached the SLA-options.xlsx with a short note in the "Dedicated" column about expected p95 ranges and preemption behavior.

Next steps: Confirm Fri 11 Sep 10:00 PT and I'll send a calendar invite w/ Rishi and our infra lead. Also please drop any sample payloads you want us to use for perf estimates.

Attachment: SLA-options.xlsx

Cheers,
Jasmine

Quick internal ask: let's prepare two MLPs for the customer: (A) Dedicated in customer VPC (preferred) and (B) Hosted + isolation add-on (fallback) with explicit tradeoffs. We'll include cost delta and operational responsibilities in both.

Thanks — Avery
